meta.methodology: Read framework.md, torah_185_packages.json, all reference===185 edges from torahData.js, and the full source text torah_185.txt. For each bechina statement in the source text, verified whether the concept appears as a node in the dataset and whether it is assigned to a package. Only concepts with explicit bechina language (בְּחִינַת, נִקְרָא, הִיא בְּחִינוֹת) were considered. Note: Torah #185 is a short, focused Torah with only 3 bechina edges in the dataset, leaving substantial bechina content from the source text unrepresented.

additions.reason: The source text states explicitly: 'הַשֵּׂכֶל נִקְרָא יוּד' (the sekhel is called yud) — this is a direct bechina statement using the language 'נִקְרָא'. The sekhel is the yud, the upper point of the letter alef, which is the first of its three structural components (yud + vav + dalet = alef = upper yir'ah). Since אות יו"ד is not separately listed as a node in the dataset for this Torah, שכל should be added as the node that fills the yud-role in the alef-structure. It is the positive intellectual dimension — God's greatness apprehended by the mind — and belongs squarely in Package 1.
additions.source_quote: הַשֵּׂכֶל נִקְרָא יוּד, כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַשִׁ"י: אָז יָשִׁיר מֹשֶׁה, שֶׁרָאוּי לִכְתֹּב שָׁר מֹשֶׁה, אֶלָּא יוּד עַל שֵׁם הַמַּחֲשָׁבָה נֶאֶמְרָה

additions.reason: The source text states: 'יִרְאָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה... הִיא בְּחִינוֹת א' — the upper/first yir'ah IS the letter alef. This is the central bechina of the entire Torah and the capstone concept: the upper fear is an aspect of alef, the complete Divine Name unit. Although an eitza edge exists for this node (id 1411: התבוננות השכל → יראה הראשונה), the bechina of יראה ראשונה = אל"ף is not recorded. This concept should be added to Package 1 to complete the picture.
additions.source_quote: יִרְאָה הָרִאשׁוֹנָה שֶׁהִיא עַל יְדֵי הִתְבּוֹנְנוּת הַשֵּׂכֶל בִּגְדֻלָּתוֹ וְרוֹמְמוּתוֹ, הִיא בְּחִינוֹת א
additions.note: Node יראה הראשונה exists in the dataset as the target of an eitza edge (id 1411, reference=185). The bechina יראה ראשונה↔אות אל"ף is present in the source text but not recorded as a bechina edge. The node exists but its bechina relationship to alef is missing.

additions.reason: The source text explicitly states: 'יִרְאָה הַשְּׁנִיָּה שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה מִדְּבָרִים תַּחְתּוֹנִים, הִיא בְּחִינַת אד' — the lower yir'ah IS a bechina of 'ad' (the word אד, mist). This is a direct bechina statement. In the dataset, this is recorded only as an eitza edge (reference=185, id=34, type=eitza). The lower yir'ah draws down shefa (blessing/abundance) into the world, functioning as העלאת מיין נוקבין. While lower than the upper yir'ah, it is still a positive (good) phenomenon — a valid lesser grade of fear that still works toward God-consciousness. This node should be assigned to Package 1 with a note that it represents the lower dimension of the same yir'ah domain.
additions.source_quote: הַיִּרְאָה הַשְּׁנִיָּה שֶׁהִיא בָּאָה מִדְּבָרִים תַּחְתּוֹנִים, הִיא בְּחִינַת אד, כִּי הִיא בְּחִינַת דַּלֵּי דָּלֶת

This may be a misclassification — 'הִיא בְּחִינַת' is bechina language, though the overall sentence describes how the lower yir'ah produces shefa.

additions.reason: The source text states: 'הוּא בְּחִינַת הַעֲלָאַת מַיִּין נֻקְבִּין' — the lower yir'ah's action IS the bechina of raising of feminine waters (a Kabbalistic term for the ascent of petition/longing that draws down divine flow). This is a direct bechina statement describing the metaphysical mechanism by which the lower yir'ah operates. It belongs in Package 1 as a descriptor of the lower yir'ah's essential nature.
additions.source_quote: עַל־יְדֵי הַיִּרְאָה זוֹ אֵינוֹ נִמְשָׁךְ רַק הַשְׁפָּעוֹת בָּעוֹלָם, כִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת הַעֲלָאַת מַיִּין נֻקְבִּין

additions.reason: The source text states: 'הַכְּלִי הִיא בְּחִינַת מֵם סְתוּמָה, וְזֶה אוֹתִיּוֹת אָדָם' — the vessel (needed to receive the drawn-down shefa) IS the bechina of the closed mem, and this is the letters of 'Adam'. This bechina (vessel = closed mem = Adam) is not in the dataset. The vessel concept is directly tied to the lower yir'ah's purpose: when lower yir'ah draws down shefa, a vessel is needed so the external forces (chitzonim) cannot feed from it. This is part of the yir'ah-shefa structure and belongs in Package 1.
additions.source_quote: וּכְשֶׁנִּמְשָׁךְ הַשֶּׁפַע, צָרִיךְ לַעֲשׂוֹת כְּלִי לְקַבֵּל הַשֶּׁפַע, שֶׁלֹּא יִינְקוּ הַחִיצוֹנִים מִמֶּנּוּ, וְהַכְּלִי הִיא בְּחִינַת מֵם סְתוּמָה, וְזֶה אוֹתִיּוֹת אָדָם

concepts_examined_and_excluded.reason: The text calls yir'ah 'סוף דבר' based on the verse from Kohelet, but this is a Scriptural citation establishing yir'ah's importance, not a bechina statement equating two conceptual nodes. The verse is used as a proof-text, not to establish a בְּחִינַת relationship.
The text says yir'ah is the עִקַּר הַשְּׁלֵמוּת (the essence of completeness), but this is a qualitative statement about yir'ah's role, not a בְּחִינַת equation between two distinct concept-nodes.

The phrase 'דַּלֵּי דָּלֶת' (doubly-poor dalet) is used to describe the lower yir'ah — it is an intensified form of the same dalet concept already in Package 1. It is a qualification of the existing אות דל"ת node rather than an independent new bechina concept.

The longing to travel to the Tzaddik is described as what creates the vessel impression (ציון/ציור). The text does not use explicit בְּחִינַת language for this concept itself — it says 'עַל יְדֵי הַהִשְׁתּוֹקְקוּת... נַעֲשֶׂה הַצִּיּוּר' (through the longing, the impression is made). This is eitza (cause-effect) language, not bechina language.

The struggles and efforts in the beginning of drawing close to God are discussed in the appended section as what creates a larger vessel. This is described causally ('עַל יְדֵי הַיְגִיעוֹת שֶׁבַּתְּחִלָּה נַעֲשֶׂה הַכְּלִי'), not using bechina language. It is an eitza relationship.

The bechina of יראה תחתונה = אד is stated inline in the source but not recorded as a separate bechina edge.
